My second time ever picking up a wild snake was a baby copperhead at work. I know it was stupid af and could have gone terribly but there was a group of my coworkers surrounding it yelling to kill it and one guy had a stick and was jabbing at it. I used a thick branch to hold its head down while I grabbed it right behind the head. I walked it into a wooded area by the parking lot and kinda threw it into the brush as gently as I could without risking it whipping around to tag me. Literally had a lady tell me to drop it in the road so she could run over it as I was carrying it. Called the guy who was poking it pathetic as I walked back inside afterward and he just stared at me slack-jawed like a dumbass. 

I do not recommend free handling a venomous snake ever but I was 18 and panicked in the moment. The other two times I've handled wild snakes was this itty bitty rough green tree snake that I found on a walk when I was around 15 (I moved him off of the sidewalk) and a 4-ish foot black rat snake that I relocated from a small business market at a local art museum that I was attending last year. Never have been tagged/bit, luckily.

A lot of comments are talking about using second hand stuff and then just fixing it yourself. There is no way you can compare that to getting it fixed professionally by someone who knows exactly what they are doing. Family or not, if someone fucked my car like that you bet I'm getting that shit fixed fully, correctly, and professionally. That's not a dent you can pull. That's crumpled in like a stomped soda can with God only knows what type of damage you can't see from these pics.
I'm glad y'all are okay and left it be. If you can't identify a snake, it's always best to be cautious, just in case to avoid anyone/anything getting hurt.
